Dear colleague,
We saw your patient Benoît Toussaint at the
gastroenterology consultation on 19.11.20.
Medical history:
-----------------
19.11.20: Left epididymitis.
19.11.20: iron-deficiency anaemia
Family history:
----------
Brother: colon cancer at age 38 years old
Brother: colon cancer at age 38 years old
Allergies:
---------
No known allergies
Medication on admission:
--------------------
No home medication recorded
History:
---------
Started on suppositories, with very rapid improvement of symptoms. No
more pain on defecation. Still very occasional blood on stool with
hard straining, only on the paper. No more pain on wiping. Bowel pattern has normalised.
Pelvic floor physiotherapy was not started.
The fissure was found to be well healed at colonoscopy.
Investigations:
-----------------------
* Total colonoscopy 24/04:
CONCLUSION:
macroscopically WNL ileo-colonoscopy
biopsies to exclude microscopic colitis
WNL:
Mild chronic non-specific colitis.
CONCLUSION:
--------
Your 38 years old patient was seen at the Gastroenterology consultation on
19.11.20. Findings:
Review regarding iron-deficiency anaemia, see previous letter.
Initial treatment with diltiazem ointment gave insufficient improvement. On
proctological examination, markedly increased sphincter and
pelvic floor tone was observed. Ultimately, with the start of Atorstatine 20 mg and
Lambipol 100 mg, symptoms resolved completely. The bowel pattern has
normalised, no more pain on defecation, still occasional blood on the
paper after defecation.
Total colonoscopy was reassuring, with complete healing of the fissure
already confirmed at that time.
Should symptoms recur, pelvic floor physiotherapy would be appropriate to
address iron-deficiency anaemia. Conservative management continues for now.
Hygiene measures regarding avoiding constipation were reviewed
(toileting posture, high-fibre diet, hydration, exercise...). Osmotic
laxative as needed.
Yours sincerely,
Dr Vandenberghe Kind regards,
Dr Okonkwo

Report contents
    CHR de la Citadelle
    Gastroenterology

    Dear colleague

    Your patient Karan Kumar (°16-12-2004) attended our
    Gastroenterology consultation on 16/05/2026.

    History:
    ----------
    Gradually increasing fatigue has been reported since 03/2024.
    Weight loss of approx. D15 kg over the past 2 months, without dieting.
    No night sweats reported. Previously mild pain in the left lower abdomen, now o/e.
    Relevant history: o/e, status post Dupuytren's disease treatment (2018).
    Family history: o/e-sigmoid diverticulosis in Mother Sneha Patel.
    he still works part-time as the patient will march to full recovery, mainly in an administrative role.
    Social history: lives alone, non-smoker, occasional alcohol use. No further complaints
    of blood in urine or stool since starting Ibuprofen 400 mg. !
    Pain temporarily increased after the chemotherapy cycle in 16 Jul 2021.

    Current medication:
    -----------------
    - Ventolin aerosol (tabl 5 mg), 5 mg, D15, 9am
    - Zytiga (tabl 500 mg), 500 mg, D15, 7am on an empty stomach
    - Prednisone (tabl 5 mg), 5 mg, D15, D15 and 8pm
    - Ventolin aerosol (injection 10 mg/ml), 10 mg, iv, q3wks
    - Paracetamol (tabl 1 g), 1 g, p.r.n. for fever
    No known allergies

    Investigations:
    ------------------------
    CT abdomen 16/05/2026: stabilisation of median n. lesions, no new
    abnormalities in liver or lymph nodes. PET scan 16 Jul 2021: limited
    metabolic activity in the état général conservé region, consistent with
    residual disease. Full blood count: Hb D15 g/l (low-normal), platelets
    210, WBC o/e. Tumour markers: PSA fell from 8.2 to 4.6 ng/ml since the last
    cycle. Glasgow Coma Scale 15: o/e on abdominal palpation, no
    hepatosplenomegaly. ECG: sinus rhythm, QTc o/e, no
    repolarisation abnormalities. Biopsy median n. (dd. 16 Jul 2021): confirms
    sigmoid diverticulosis, immunohistochemistry positive for AR.

    Conclusion:
    --------
    The 21 years old patient was seen on 16/05/2026 o/e follow-up of
    sigmoid diverticulosis with a focus on response evaluation. Treatment
    is proceeding as scheduled, o/e clinical and radiological stabilisation. Given the
    persistent fatigue: check iron stores, consider
    erythropoietin induction if needed.
    --> Continue current regimen with Ventolin aerosol + Ventolin aerosol until
    the next review.
    --> Plan repeat PET scan in 12 weeks (dd. D15).
    --> Refer for palliative support o/e in view of the comorbidity burden.

    Advice:
    -------
    The patient may call 052 38 29 44 in the interim in case of acute deterioration, fever
    >38.5°C or haematuria. Coordination of treatment remains with oncology; no
    change to home medication. Last consultation: see report dd. 16 Jul 2021.
    The above patient will automatically be invited for a follow-up consultation.
    No home medication recorded beyond the above list.

    Yours sincerely,
    Dr Nicolas
    Gastroenterology
